title: Boxers Sam Langford, Jack Johnson and Henry Armstrong
summary: He never met Jack Johnson, but was a buddy of fighter Sam Langford and recalls Gunboat Smith and Henry Armstrong watching him play.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Did you ever know anything about Jack Johnson?

Jack Johnson? Jack Johnson I never met, but he was -- up in 1914, he was up there in Chelsea, Massachusetts. But I didn't see him, see. And I think Sam Langford -- see, I used to be a buddy of Sam Langford's.
Sam Langford was a heavyweight fighter. He and Gus Smith used to fight each other.
No, he was a white guy. And they used to fight, put on a --
No, this was a real fight. One would win this day and the next one would win -- I said, why don't you keep them -- he said, well, we've got to get along. Out

Revere Beach, I used to go out there with Sam Langford and walk with him, and Henry Armstrong. Henry Armstrong was in New York, and he used to come down to the theater there where he heard us, and watch us. Man, if I could play piano like you. I said, oh, you. If I could fight like you, I said.
